value_domain: Census 2021 Australian Defence Force service, detailed (8 categories)

variable_description: Australian Defence Force service reported at the 2021 Census, split by regular against reserves and by current against previous service. The ABS defines it as "The Australian Defence Force (ADF) consists of regulars and reservists, and this variable provides a detailed breakdown of current and previous service for both", and it is new in 2021, so the ACLD data item list marks the 2011 and 2016 columns "Not available". ADFP_21 on the same row is the four-category summary of the same answer, and both are asked only of people aged 15 years and over.

limitation: It cannot date or measure service. The categories say whether service happened, not when it began, how long it ran or whether it was broken, and the ABS notes the variable does not capture breaks in service. Because there is no 2011 or 2016 column, a person cannot be tracked into or out of the ADF across the ACLD panel; 2021 is the only observation.
rationale: The 2021 Census Dictionary page gives the definition, the eight categories and the statement that the variable is new for 2021, and the ACLD data item list supplies the ACLD-specific 97/98/99 codes.

value_domain: Census 2021 Australian Defence Force service (4 categories)

value_domain: Census 2021 count of selected long-term health conditions (0, 1, 2, 3 or more)
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Count of selected long-term health conditions (CLTHP)
variable_description: How many of ten named long-term health conditions the person reported at the 2021 Census, the first Census to ask the question. The dictionary defines it as "the number of selected long-term health conditions a person has reported", the ten being arthritis, asthma, cancer, dementia, diabetes, heart disease, kidney disease, lung condition, mental health condition and stroke. There is no 2011 or 2016 counterpart in the ACLD because the question is new for 2021, so this column cannot open a health trajectory that starts at an earlier wave.

The 2016 dictionary, which first defined it, calls it "a housing utilisation measure based upon a comparison of the number of bedrooms in a dwelling together with a series of household demographics such as the number of usual residents, their relationship to one another, their age and sex". It was not a standard Census output variable in 2011, being "a new derived item for 2016", so the 2011 value in the ACLD is the same derivation applied retrospectively to 2011 records.

value_domain: Census unpaid domestic work hours band (2011)
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Unpaid Domestic Work: Number of Hours (DOMP)
variable_description: Hours the person spent on unpaid domestic work in the week before the 2011 Census, in five broad bands. The 2011 Census Dictionary defines it as, "For each person aged 15 years and over, records the number of hours spent performing unpaid domestic work. It includes work that the person did without pay, in their own home and in other places, for themselves, their family and other people in the household, in the week prior to Census Night." The question, the reference week and the five bands are unchanged at 2016 and 2021, so DOMP_11, DOMP_16 and DOMP_21 form a comparable series.

The measure also covers only the single week before Census night, so a person who was ill, travelling or on holiday that week records a figure that is not their usual pattern.
rationale: The 2011 Census Dictionary is the authority for the 2011 wave of this panel, and its DOMP entry supplies the definition, the reference week, the age scope and the exact band boundaries.
evidence_quote: For each person aged 15 years and over, records the number of hours spent performing unpaid domestic work.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the custodian's label 'Unpaid Domestic Work: Number of Hours' and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, so a reader could not tell that the answer is a band rather than a count of hours, or that the reference period is one week.

value_domain: Census unpaid domestic work hours band (2021)

evidence_quote: Calculated by summing the personal incomes reported by all family members aged 15 years and over.

value_domain: Census weekly family income range

variable_description: The sampled person's 2016 family income, left uncalculated when the family was not fully reported. The 2016 Census Dictionary states the rule directly: "Total Family Income (weekly) is not calculated where a family member aged 15 years and over did not state their income, or was temporarily absent." The Partial income stated and All incomes not stated codes work as they did in 2011, but the dollar bands do not: the ABS redrew the family income ranges for 2016, taking FINF from seventeen bands with a $5,000-or-more top band to twenty-two topping out at $8,000 or more.

limitation: The banding, not just the missingness, limits what can be done with it. Because each member contributes an assigned median rather than a reported dollar figure, family totals cannot support inequality measures that depend on the shape of the distribution within a band, and a small real change will often not move a family across a boundary at all.
rationale: The 2016 dictionary chapter states the non-calculation rule explicitly and lists the bands and special codes, which is the difference between this column and the as-stated one beside it.
evidence_quote: Total Family Income (weekly) is not calculated where a family member aged 15 years and over did not state their income, or was temporarily absent.

value_domain: Census family composition code
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. no. 2901.0), Family Composition (FMCF)
variable_description: The type of family the sampled person belonged to at the 2011 Census: couple with or without children, one parent, or other family. The 2011 Census Dictionary defines it as classifying "families into different types", and adds that "information about temporarily absent family members is used" when the type is worked out, so a child away on Census Night still counts. The detail levels split couple and one-parent families by whether children under 15, dependent students or non-dependent children are present.

limitation: A family here is a set of related people in one dwelling, so it cannot see a family spread across two. Separated parents and their children form two families in different households, shared-care children appear in only one of them, and an adult living alone is not a one-person family but a non-family household coded not applicable.
rationale: The 2011 dictionary chapter for FMCF gives the definition, the treatment of temporarily absent members and the four-level category hierarchy for the Census year the _11 suffix names.
evidence_quote: Family Composition classifies families into different types. When classifying families into different types, information about temporarily absent family members is used.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label 'Family Composition' and the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so it never said that the family is defined within a single dwelling.

value_domain: Census family composition code
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. no. 2901.0), Family Composition (FMCF)

The 2016 Census Dictionary states the mechanism plainly: "Families are classified in terms of the relationships that exist between a single family reference person and each other member of that family." The category structure is unchanged from 2011, so the codes are directly comparable, but the reference person is chosen afresh at each Census and the classification depends on who that is.

A young adult who stops being a dependent student, a child who turns 15, or a different person being taken as the family reference person will all move the code without anyone entering or leaving the family.
rationale: The 2016 dictionary chapter states the reference-person mechanism and shows the categories are unchanged from 2011, which is what governs how the two ACLD waves can be compared.
evidence_quote: Families are classified in terms of the relationships that exist between a single family reference person and each other member of that family.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and gave no hint that the classification is built around a reference person who can change between waves.

value_domain: Census public/private sector code
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. no. 2901.0), Public/Private Employer Indicator (GNGP)
variable_description: Whether the sampled person's employer at the 2011 Census was in the public or the private sector. The 2011 Census Dictionary explains the derivation: "The employer's business name and the workplace address of the employed person is used to classify employed persons into the public or private sector." Nobody answered a question about sector, so this is an ABS coding decision made from written employer details, and it splits the public sector into national, state or territory, and local government.

Where an employer cannot be established as public it is coded private, so private counts absorb unresolved and badly written employer names and public sector counts are a floor rather than an estimate. The code also describes the employer, not the work: a cleaner contracted into a public hospital is private here.
rationale: The 2011 dictionary chapter states how the classification is derived from employer name and workplace address, lists the codes and defines the not applicable population.
evidence_quote: The employer's business name and the workplace address of the employed person is used to classify employed persons into the public or private sector.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label 'Public/Private Employer Indicator' with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, and gave no warning that unresolved employers default to the private sector.

The 2011 dictionary records that the variable was renamed from Household Income - Equivalised (weekly) and that its categories were revised and some codes amended for 2011, so the 2011 bands do not line up with 2006. Children absent on Census Night are included in the equivalence factor while visitors are excluded, and HIED is not calculated for visitor-only households.

In the real asset the ACLD is a five per cent random sample of people counted on Census night, carried forward using "a mix of deterministic and probabilistic linkage methodologies", with the 2016 and 2021 Censuses also linked to the ABS person linkage spine. In fplida the value is generated rather than derived from anyone, but it behaves like the real key: one value per sampled person, stable across every column on the row.
value_definition: An opaque identifier with no meaning in its digits. It is not a Census form number, not a household number, and not decodable back to a person, so it can be matched but not read.
limitation: It does not tell you whether the person linked at every wave. A row exists for each sampled person, and a wave where linkage failed looks in the data exactly like a wave where the person had died, left the country or was missed by the Census, so missing 2021 columns must not be read as attrition from Australia. It is also a person key and not a family key: two members of one couple sampled independently carry unrelated values and nothing here shows they lived together.
rationale: The ABS ACLD microdata page describes the sample fraction, the waves and the deterministic and probabilistic linkage that this key stands in for, and states that the 2016 and 2021 Censuses were linked to the person linkage spine.
evidence_quote: a mix of deterministic and probabilistic linkage methodologies
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Synthetic person ID for ACLD record' with the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so it never said what the key joins or that a missing wave is a linkage outcome rather than a life event.

value_domain: Census 2011 tenure type (TEND) code
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Tenure Type (TEND)
variable_description: Whether the private dwelling the person lived in at the 2011 Census was owned outright, owned with a mortgage, rented or held some other way. The dictionary's definition is that the variable "Describes whether a dwelling is owned, being purchased or rented. Dwellings occupied under a life tenure scheme can be considered as being owned." It is an attribute of the dwelling carried on the person's row, and TENLLD_P_11 breaks the rented category down by landlord.
value_definition: A one-character code: 1 owned outright; 2 owned with a mortgage; 3 being purchased under a rent/buy scheme; 4 rented; 5 being occupied rent-free; 6 being occupied under a life tenure scheme; 7 other tenure type; & not stated; @ not applicable. The population is occupied private dwellings.
limitation: Code 3 reads as a rent/buy scheme in 2011 and a shared equity scheme from 2016; the ABS treats this as a relabel of the same category, so the wording changes between waves but the group does not. Tenure belongs to the dwelling and not to the person: a boarder or an adult child in an owner-occupied house carries owned outright, which makes this column a poor proxy for whether the individual is a homeowner.
rationale: The 2011 chapter for TEND gives the definition, the applicable population of occupied private dwellings and the complete 2011 code list including the rent/buy label that later changed.
evidence_quote: Describes whether a dwelling is owned, being purchased or rented. Dwellings occupied under a life tenure scheme can be considered as being owned.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed the custodian's 'Tenure Type' and the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so it named no Census year, gave no codes and did not warn that tenure describes the dwelling rather than the person.

value_domain: Census 2016 tenure type (TEND) code
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Tenure Type (TEND)
variable_description: Whether the private dwelling the person lived in at the 2016 Census was owned outright, owned with a mortgage, rented or held some other way. The 2016 dictionary shortens the definition to a variable that "Describes whether a dwelling is owned, being purchased or rented." and relabels code 3 from a rent/buy scheme to a shared equity scheme. The remaining categories match 2011, so the ownership and rental splits are comparable across the two waves.
value_definition: A one-character code: 1 owned outright; 2 owned with a mortgage; 3 being purchased under a shared equity scheme; 4 rented; 5 being occupied rent-free; 6 being occupied under a life tenure scheme; 7 other tenure type; & not stated; @ not applicable.

evidence_quote: Describes whether a dwelling is owned, being purchased or rented.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Tenure Type' with the generic no-value-list sentence duplicated, so it gave neither the Census year nor the change in the code 3 label since 2011.

value_domain: Count of children ever born, 00 to 30
value_source: ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Number of Children Ever Born (TISP)
variable_description: The number of children a woman reported ever having borne, as recorded at the 2011 Census. The dictionary defines it as a variable that "Records the number of children ever born (live births) to each female.", and the 2011 form still carried the instruction to count live births only, which was removed for 2016. It applies to females aged 15 years and over; TISRP_11 holds the same count in bands.
value_definition: A two-digit count from 00 for no children through 29, with 30 standing for thirty or more children. The residual codes are && not stated, @@ not applicable and VV overseas visitor, and not applicable covers males and females under 15 years.

Because the live-births instruction was dropped after 2011, a rise between TISP_11 and TISP_16 for the same woman can reflect the changed instruction rather than another birth, which matters in a longitudinal file where the same person is observed twice.
rationale: The 2011 chapter for TISP gives the definition including the live births wording, the applicable population and the full numeric code range, and the 2021 page records that the instruction was removed in 2016.
evidence_quote: Records the number of children ever born (live births) to each female.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's 'Number of Children Ever Born' with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so it named no Census year and did not mention the instruction change that makes 2011 different from later waves.
